response: Preventing osteoporosis is a crucial step in reducing the risk of aromatase inhibitor-related musculoskeletal symptoms. Patients on aromatase inhibitors (AIs) who develop osteoporosis are at an increased risk of musculoskeletal symptoms and bone fractures. Comedication with calcium and bisphosphonates (Ca/Bis) can reduce the likelihood of osteoporosis and musculoskeletal symptoms. Additionally, patients who received tamoxifen before starting AIs were less likely to develop AI-related musculoskeletal symptoms. Therefore, it is recommended that patients on AIs be offered Ca/Bis to reduce the incidence of musculoskeletal symptoms and fractures, especially if they are receiving steroidal AIs and/or did not receive tamoxifen before starting AIs. By preventing osteoporosis, healthcare providers can help alleviate aromatase inhibitor-related musculoskeletal symptoms and improve the overall quality of life for patients undergoing treatment.
